iterationLog.purpose: Every case that did not pass on first implementation, with the true root cause and the fix actually applied. Per Sections 21/22/29's anti-gaming discipline, no fix here ever loosened SAFE_SURFACING_REQUIRES_SEMANTIC_CORRESPONDENCE or any dimension threshold - every fix corrected a test-authoring inaccuracy (an unrealistic synthetic fixture) or corrected a wrong hand-authored expectation, verified against the evaluator's own documented design in matching.ts and Section 13-15's discovery-vs-representation discipline.

cases.trueRootCause: TWO test-authoring defects, not an evaluator defect: (1) the candidate lacked declaredRole:'DEFINITION', so extractPosture() had no declared-type fallback and the candidate's paraphrase ('occurs when... comes to beneficially own') does not match DEFINITION_RE's word list (means/shall mean/has the meaning/is defined as/definition of), leaving posture UNDETERMINED where a real compiled/discovered DEFINITION candidate would carry provisionRoleDeclared='DEFINITION' (confirmed real-pipeline pattern: lib/contract-model/evaluation-v2/adapters/dsgr.ts:405). (2) The GT's own drafting used the word 'acquisition' in a Change-of-Control definition ('the acquisition by any Person... of beneficial ownership'); ACTION_PATTERNS' generic acquisition regex (signals.ts) fired ACQUIRE_BUSINESS on this bare word regardless of legal context, so the GT carried a spurious M&A-style action tag that the (correctly action-less) candidate paraphrase could never match, and the pairing was reported as materially conflicting (WRONG_ACTION) rather than merely equally silent on action.
cases.fix: Test-only: added declaredRole:'DEFINITION' to the candidate (mirrors real DEFINITION-candidate construction) and reworded the GT/candidate text to describe the same Change-of-Control mechanic without the word 'acquisition' (both sides now correctly resolve A_SUBJECT_ACTION to NOT_APPLICABLE). No evaluator code touched.
cases.disclosedFinding: Discovered along the way: ACTION_PATTERNS' acquisition regex (the same generalized mechanism already implicated in 03-definition-overmatch-root-cause.json) can also spuriously tag a Change-of-Control / equity-ownership-acquisition DEFINITION with ACQUIRE_BUSINESS purely from the bare word 'acquisition', independent of the excerpt-resolution defect already fixed in source-excerpt.ts. This is a second, distinct instance of the same class of defect (a keyword-only ACTION_PATTERNS regex with no legal-context discrimination) as the already-disclosed, deliberately-unfixed EXERCISE_REMEDIES overbreadth. Not fixed in this phase for the same reason (broad, cross-corpus blast radius; not validated within this phase's budget) - see 16-remaining-evaluator-risks.json.

cases.trueRootCause: Test-authoring defect. The candidate's text was written as a pure meta-narrative ('...could not be confidently resolved because...') with no actual clause content, so B_LEGAL_POSTURE and E_ECONOMICS had nothing to detect. Real HONEST_UNRESOLVED candidates carry the ACTUAL raw clause excerpt in `excerpts` (adapters/dsgr.ts:317, `excerpt = u.excerptText`) with diagnostic reasoning layered on separately - the self-report role is metadata on top of real content, not a substitute for it.
cases.fix: Test-only: rewrote the candidate's text to lead with the actual substantive clause ('The Total Net Leverage Ratio shall not exceed the level set forth in the Pricing Grid...') and append the honest-uncertainty language, matching how real self-report candidates are actually constructed. No evaluator code touched.

cases.trueRootCause: Same test-authoring defect as SS18: candidate text was pure diagnostic narrative with no restated definition, so DEFINITION_RE never fired and B_LEGAL_POSTURE stayed UNDETERMINED.
cases.fix: Test-only: candidate now restates the formula ('...means the ratio of Consolidated EBITDA minus Capital Expenditures...') with declaredRole:'DEFINITION', then appends the honest-unsupported declaration. No evaluator code touched.

cases.initialFailure: Test asserted dangerousUnaccounted:false; evaluator returned true.
cases.trueRootCause: The test's own expectation was substantively wrong, not the evaluator. Section 13-15 of this phase's own charter is explicit: discovery must never be conflated with representation, and safe surfacing is a distinct, narrower category than mere discovery (INVENTORY_ONLY is not one of the accountingRoles - HONEST_UNRESOLVED / HONEST_UNSUPPORTED / SAFETY_FLAG - that matching.ts treats as an honest, user-visible safety declaration). A fully-corresponding INVENTORY_ONLY candidate proves the system noticed the provision; it does not prove the user was ever told the claim lacks representation. matching.ts's own terminal branch (the 'every corresponding candidate is inventory-only' case) correctly returns UNREPRESENTED with explicitlySurfacedAsUnsafe:false, and the aggregate layer correctly keeps this DANGEROUS_UNACCOUNTED - exactly the discovery-vs-representation separation Section 15 requires be preserved, not redefined.
cases.fix: Test-only: corrected the expectation to dangerousUnaccounted:true and rewrote the case description to state the correct invariant (discovery-only correspondence is preserved as 'surfacedByInventoryOnly' for provenance, but never suppresses DANGEROUS_UNACCOUNTED). No evaluator code touched.

cases.initialFailure: First iteration: matchStatus=UNREPRESENTED (candidates' paraphrases lacked deontic language, e.g. dropped 'must', so B_LEGAL_POSTURE was UNDETERMINED on both). Second iteration (after fixing posture wording): matchStatus=EXACT_SINGLE instead of AMBIGUOUS, because the two paraphrase candidates were judged `reconcilable()` (matching.ts) - same document, same posture, no conflicting MONEY/PERCENT/RATIO figures - so they merged into one composite match instead of competing.
cases.trueRootCause: Test-design defect, not an evaluator defect: two differently-worded paraphrases of the SAME fact are, correctly, evidence for a composite match, not ambiguity. matching.ts's AMBIGUOUS state (see the file's own header comment) is reserved for candidates that are MUTUALLY IRRECONCILABLE - i.e. they assert genuinely conflicting content (different figures, different postures) that the GT claim itself is silent on, exactly the shape already proven correct by the pre-existing A22-ambiguous-cluster case in adversarial-cases.ts (two $-denominated baskets with different dollar caps).
cases.fix: Test-only: replaced the reinstatement-mechanic scenario with a structurally different-but-analogous case explicitly modeled on A22 - a single covenant (equity repurchase basket) with two candidates identical except for a conflicting dollar cap ($5,000,000 vs $20,000,000), which the GT itself does not specify. This correctly produces AMBIGUOUS. Also corrected a second wrong expectation: dangerousUnaccounted was originally asserted false on the theory that 'correctly detecting ambiguity' should count as safe; this is not what the architecture does or should do - AMBIGUOUS is not a self-declared safety flag (no HONEST_UNRESOLVED/HONEST_UNSUPPORTED/SAFETY_FLAG candidate is present), so it correctly remains DANGEROUS_UNACCOUNTED. The corrected expectation (dangerousUnaccounted:true) matches the implicit, already-tested behavior of A22. No evaluator code touched.
